limitations: This was a local frozen-render audit; no HTTP/live website review was performed.

Mathematical review was limited to rendering-sensitive notation, diagram presence and mathematical relations relevant to the suggested DAG, and visible title/ItemBody content; it is not a general proof audit.
No title contained raw TeX markers or ASCII subscript/superscript syntax warranting an optional typography finding.
limitations_on_clipping: All 81 tiles were opened separately at original resolution. No clipping defect was confirmed; partial content at tile boundaries continued in the next separately reviewed tile.

candidates.exact_claim: The binary SCM has U→A, U→Y, A→M, M→Y; the only directed A-to-Y path passes through M, A←U→Y←M is blocked at collider Y in G_underlined A, and M←A←U→Y is blocked by A for the other front-door condition.
candidates.why_warranted: The graph topology and two path-blocking conditions are the example’s central structure; a small DAG would make the common cause, mediator, collider, and intervention-cut relation easy to check at a glance.
candidates.specific_content: Draw four vertices U, A, M, Y with directed edges U→A, U→Y, A→M, and M→Y. Mark M as the mediator and show the directed path A→M→Y. Indicate that the backdoor path A←U→Y←M is closed at collider Y, while the path M←A←U→Y is closed by conditioning on A for the second front-door requirement. If showing G_underlined A, remove outgoing arrows from A and label that mutilated graph explicitly. Keep the source’s two distinct separation claims and do not imply that the graph alone establishes numerical identification.
candidates.evidence_note: The separately opened tile contains the graph and path conditions as prose, with no existing diagram; the proposed edges and blockers come directly from the frozen example.
